Add a styled layer and its legend to a MapLibre GL map

Source: R/gq_mapgl_layer.R
gq_mapgl_layer.Rd

Draws one sf layer on a gq web map, styled from a registry key, from classes the caller names, or from one colour, and adds its categorical legend tied to the layer, so the legend hides when the layer is switched off in gq_mapgl_controls().

Usage

gq_mapgl_layer(
  map,
  id,
  x = NULL,
  source = id,
  key = NULL,
  classes = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  reg = NULL,
  field = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  widths = c(0.6, 3),
  radius = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  legend = TRUE,
  legend_title = id,
  popup = NULL,
  visible = TRUE,
  digits = 5L,
  ...
)

Arguments

map

A map from gq_mapgl_basemap().

id

The layer id: what gq_mapgl_controls() switches, and the legend's layer_id.

x

An sf to draw, or NULL to draw a source already on the map. gq checks the data a layer draws: its geometry, and that every column the style or popup reads is there. A source it cannot read without fetching it (vector tiles, PMTiles, a GeoJSON URL) is drawn unchecked, and needs type unless key gives it. Its coordinates are taken to EPSG:4326 and rounded to digits; keep only the columns the style and popup read, since every one is written into the page.

source

The source id. Defaults to id; name an existing source with x = NULL to draw it again.

key

A registry layer key, such as "lake" or "bec_zone".

classes

Classes the caller names, a list of field (the column), values (the values matched), colors (one per value), and optionally labels (the legend's names, default values) and default (the colour of anything else, default "#cccccc").

color

One colour for every feature, when there is no key or classes.

reg

A registry, as from gq_reg_main(); read only with key.

field

Overrides the registry layer's classification field, as in gq_style(), when the data names the column differently. A registry layer's legend lists only the classes found in this column of x.

type

"line", "fill" or "circle". Read from the data's geometry when not given; a type given must agree with it, except "line" over polygons, which draws their outlines.

width

A line width in pixels, a MapLibre expression, or the name of a stream order column, which draws order 1 at widths[1] pixels and order 6 and above at widths[2].

widths

Width in pixels at order 1 and at order 6, for a width column.

radius

A circle radius in pixels, or a MapLibre expression such as one that grows with zoom.

opacity

An opacity for every feature, overriding the registry's.

legend

Add the layer's legend.

legend_title

The legend's title, or for one colour the row's name. Defaults to id.

popup

A column name, or the expr of gq_mapgl_popup().

visible

FALSE adds the layer switched off.

digits

Decimal places kept in the coordinates; 5 is about 1 m.

...

Further arguments to the mapgl layer function, such as circle_stroke_color, filter or before_id.

Value

map, with the layer and its legend added.

Details

Several layers can draw one source: pass the data once with x, then add the next layer with x = NULL and the same source. Each layer is a separate switch, as in a map that colours one set of segments two ways.

Colours are given to MapLibre as hex. R colour names such as grey80 draw in tmap but MapLibre cannot read them and drops the whole layer, so they are converted here.

Legends stack down the top-left corner in the order the layers were added, and a hidden layer's legend leaves no gap. mapgl draws every legend at the corner itself, one over another, so gq adds a stylesheet beside the map that lets them flow. A one-colour layer's legend is a single row named by legend_title, with no title above it.

See also

gq_mapgl_popup(), gq_mapgl_controls(), gq_mapgl_classes()

Examples

obs <- neexdzii_fish_obs
m <- gq_mapgl_basemap(neexdzii_wsd, "positron") |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("lakes", neexdzii_lakes["gnis_name_1"], key = "lake",
                 reg = gq_reg_main(), legend_title = "Lake") |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("Coho", obs[obs$species_code == "CO", "species_code"],
                 color = "#FF7F00", radius = 6) |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("Rainbow trout", obs[obs$species_code == "RB", "species_code"],
                 color = "steelblue", radius = 6)
vapply(m$x$layers, `[[`, "", "id")
#> [1] "lakes"         "Coho"          "Rainbow trout"
m$x$layers[[3]]$paint[["circle-color"]]     # a colour name, sent as hex
#> [1] "#4682B4"
